heard: An icy moon near Uranus once erupted liquid water. Astronomer William LaSalle discovered Ariel in 1851. Ariel has the youngest, most reflective surface of Uranus' major moons. NASA's Voyager 2 flew past up close in 1986. Photos revealed deep fault valleys slicing across smooth plains. Those smooth plains formed when molten ice erupted across its crust. Scientists even detected carbon dioxide frozen on the surface. Recent studies suggest a liquid ocean hides beneath its icy shell. But hidden warmth keeps Ariel active far longer than expected.
